description.short: Robust, malty Hunan black tea with a historic legacy in the overland tea trade to Russia via Kyakhta
description.overview: From one of the oldest black tea producing regions in China, whose harvest historically traveled along the overland Great Tea Road to Russia and Mongolia.
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling → full oxidation → drying, traditionally with a touch of gentle smoking

history.origin: Anhua County has long been a historical tea center in Hunan, initially renowned for dark tea (heicha), and producing black tea since the 19th century
history.development: In the 18th and 19th centuries, tea from this region was heavily exported along the overland 'Great Tea Road' through Kyakhta to Russia, alongside compressed dark teas from the same county
history.modern: Today less prominent internationally than Keemun or Dian Hong, but remains an important and respected regional category of Chinese black tea
interestingFacts: Anhua County is unique in producing both famous dark teas (Fu Zhuan, Tian Jian) and black tea (Hu Hong) — a rare coexistence of two major fermented tea traditions in a single county
Historically, Hunan black tea formed a substantial portion of overland exports to Russia alongside teas from Hubei
